title: When the Uniform Burns
premise: In the winter of a collapsing republic, Lior Eastwick carries sealed diplomatic codes aboard the last river steamer bound for neutral territory — but the census taker who boards at Vellmark is no clerk, and the codes are worth more than the ship itself. As ice closes on the river and passengers turn informant against passenger, Lior discovers the 'family' they've protected for ten years is built on a stolen inheritance of names, papers, and one true heir's erased identity. When only one berth remains on the final lifeboat before the river freezes solid, Lior must choose between the woman who raised them under false papers and the stranger whose name was taken to make their family possible. In the end, Lior gives up the berth themselves, burns the codes unread, and walks north across the ice with both women — choosing truth over loyalty, and finding that family survives neither lie nor inheritance, only choice.
about_author: Gideon Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing displaced-persons records from border regions, an experience that haunts every page of this novel. They write from a farmhouse near a frozen river, where they claim the ice still sounds like breaking promises.

chapters.title: The Question That Wasn't on the Form
chapters.summary: Lior Eastwick's POV. A routine census interview in the boarding house at Vellmark turns when the census taker asks about 'the year of the crossing' — a question no legitimate form contains. Lior lies smoothly, but recognizes the trap being set. Emotional beat: ten years of practiced silence cracking under a single question.

chapters.title: Codes in a Coat Liner
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, flashback woven into present. We learn Lior is courier for the dying republic's last diplomatic mission, carrying cipher codes sewn into a coat once owned by their dead mother. The steamer Merrow departs at dawn. Beat: dread disguised as duty; Lior memorizes faces at the dock, including the census taker's.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Raised a Ghost
chapters.summary: Maren Eastwick's POV. Maren reflects on raising Lior under borrowed identity papers after the purge, and her fear that the census inquiry has reached the shipping lines. She bribes a purser. Beat: fierce, guilty love — she knows the family she built stands on someone else's erased name.

chapters.title: Passengers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A gallery of souls aboard: a defected judge, twin brothers fleeing conscription, a singer with contraband sheet music, and Sable Voss, a quiet woman who watches Lior too carefully. The census taker boards under a second name. Beat: claustrophobic intimacy; everyone is lying about something.

chapters.title: What the Ice Hears
chapters.summary: Sable Voss's POV. Sable reveals (to the reader) she is the true heir whose identity was erased to create Lior's papers — hired by the census bureau to find 'her own' documents. She doesn't yet know Lior wears her name. Beat: cold purpose beginning to thaw into doubt.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Betrayal
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The judge is denounced by one of the twins and removed at a midriver stop. Lior realizes informants are being cultivated among passengers — and that the census taker offered Maren immunity in exchange for the codes. Beat: the ship becomes a confession chamber; trust starts dying.

chapters.title: Maren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren confesses partially to Lior: the papers were bought from a broker who 'retired' a girl named Sable Voss to make room for them. She never knew if the girl lived. Beat: guilt as inheritance; Maren begs Lior never to look for the ghost.

chapters.title: The Singer's Price
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, Lior's POV. The singer trades information for coal rations, naming Sable as a bureau agent. Lior confronts Sable at the rail in the freezing fog; neither tells the whole truth, but each recognizes the other's loneliness. Beat: dangerous kinship between two people made of false papers.

chapters.title: River Narrowing
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ice floes thicken; the captain announces they may not beat the freeze to the neutral port. Sable intercepts a telegram confirming the republic has fallen — the codes are now the only thing left of its legitimacy. Beat: vertigo of serving a country that no longer exists.

chapters.title: The Berth List
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The purser posts the lifeboat manifest: four berths, nine claimants, priority by 'verified identity.' Verification means papers — which means Lior's forged name could save or doom them. Beat: bureaucratic horror; identity becomes literal survival currency.

chapters.title: Confession at the Boiler
chapters.summary: Dual tension, Lior's POV. In the boiler room's heat, Sable tells Lior her name was stolen twenty years ago — not knowing she's speaking to its current wearer. Lior says nothing. Beat: the cruelest silence of Lior's life, chosen to keep Maren safe.

chapters.title: What Maren Burned
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Flashback to the night Maren took infant Lior and the broker's papers, leaving the real child's record to burn. She reveals she kept one page — proof of Sable's existence — hidden in the same coat lining as the codes. Beat: love and theft indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Census Taker's Offer
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The census taker corners Lior: surrender the codes and all three of them get berths and amnesty. He knows everything — the papers, the theft, even Sable's true name. Beat: temptation weaponized; the offer is generous, which makes it monstrous.

chapters.title: Twin Ice
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable discovers the coat lining's double secret — codes and proof of her own existence — while Lior sleeps. She holds both in her hands for a long hour. Beat: mirrored temptation; she can destroy Lior or complete herself, not both.

chapters.title: The River Stops
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Lior's POV. The Merrow grinds into pack ice twelve miles short of the port. Panic, rationing, the captain's grim arithmetic. The twins fight over a berth; the judge's denouncer is shunned. Beat: civilization thinning to its threads; the berth list becomes law.

chapters.title: Three Names, One Coat
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior confesses everything to Sable: the stolen name, Maren's bargain, the codes. Sable's response is not rage but exhaustion — 'I just want to have been real.' Beat: grief as recognition; enemies becoming something like sisters.

chapters.title: Maren's Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren accepts the census taker's deal alone, planning to trade herself and the codes for Lior's berth. Lior intercepts the exchange and burns the codes in the boiler fire before his eyes. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made literal — the mission dies so the people might live.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Lior/Sable POV. The ice cracks; one berth remains. Maren puts Lior in it; Lior climbs out and puts Sable in; Sable refuses until Lior speaks the words that settle it: 'It was always your name.' Sable takes the boat. Beat: sacrifice as restitution — the inheritance returned.

chapters.title: Walking North
chapters.summary: Lior and Maren's POV, interleaved. Mother and child walk the ice toward the shore lights, expecting arrest, finding instead the census taker gone — his own papers, it turns out, were borrowed too. Beat: bitter mercy; everyone in this story was someone else's forgery.

chapters.title: What the Boat Carried
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, arriving at the neutral port. She registers under her own name for the first time, then petitions the consulate to recognize two refugees: Maren and Lior Eastwick — 'family by declaration.' Beat: found family formalized through the very bureaucracy that unmade them.

chapters.title: Reunion on Neutral Ground
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Spring thaw; the three reunite at a border hostel. Maren gives Lior the burned coat's last scrap — not the codes, but Sable's original birth record, restored. Beat: quiet joy; inheritance redefined as memory freely given.

chapters.title: The New Census
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Lior's POV, years later. A new census taker asks Lior's household their names. Lior answers with all three — true ones — and adds a fourth line: 'and one we chose.' Beat: resolution; the silences that kept them safe are finally spent, and speech keeps them safer.
